C-RELEASE-CANARY-PRERELEASE.Summary: Publish owner-created hyphenated tags (beta/canary) as signed GitHub prereleases for external testers without advancing the stable updater feed, the GitHub latest pointer, or the Homebrew cask.
C-RELEASE-CANARY-PRERELEASE.Problem: The release workflow's publish stage unconditionally clears the prerelease flag, requires that releases/latest advance to the tag, and runs the Homebrew cask handoff. A hyphenated tag pushed through the current pipeline therefore reaches every stable user through the in-app updater. There is no sanctioned way to hand a signed, notarized pre-release build of a collecting train to an external tester: the manual-build job is unsigned and discards its artifacts, and hand-built DMGs (the TokMo pattern) carry Gatekeeper friction and per-iteration manual work.

Goals.Goal: A hyphenated SemVer tag (vX.Y.Z-beta.N or vX.Y.Z-canary.N) created through the owner tag mechanism builds with the same signing and notarization lanes as a stable release and publishes as a GitHub prerelease that never becomes the repository's latest release.

Stable-channel invariants hold for every prerelease publication: releases/latest and the updater feed (latest.json and the counting-gateway URLs) still point at the previous stable tag, and the publish-cask job does not run.

Prerelease assets include the macOS DMG and the Windows installer under the same WINDOWS_RELEASE staging variable as stable releases, so external testers on both platforms install from direct asset links.
Prerelease publication stays owner-gated exactly like stable publication: the tag app creates the tag, and the synchronous release Environment approval exposes the draft.
Release train documentation (release-trains README boundary note, release process) states that a prerelease tag is not a train dispatch, needs no Ready seal, and records no acceptance.

Constraints.Constraint: The five train rules stand: a prerelease tag may bind to a Collecting-train commit; readiness/Ready-seal is intentionally not required for it; nothing in this change dispatches or publishes a train.
The stable path stays byte-identical for non-hyphenated tags: prerelease flag cleared, feed-advance verification, cask handoff, materials checks.
The edit is actionlint-clean; no new secrets, environments, or permissions; signing stays inside the tag-restricted release-signing environment.
Immutable-release guarantees are preserved: draft-first publication, digest verification, no clobbering of published assets, no tag retargeting.
Repository artifacts stay in English; the prerelease notes body is a generated short summary, not reviewed release materials.

NonGoals.NonGoal: A separate canary updater feed, an in-app channel switcher, or scheduled nightly automation — a future change if direct-link installs stop being sufficient for testers.
Making any prerelease the GitHub latest release or advancing /releases/latest to it.
Homebrew cask, winget, App Store, or TestFlight publication of prereleases.
Reviewed release materials (What's New cards, screenshot manifests) for prereleases.
Changing the in-app updater client, its endpoint, or its rollback guards.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: For a hyphenated-tag run, gh release view reports isDraft=false and isPrerelease=true, and gh api repos/xronocode/mark/releases/latest still returns the previous stable tag after publication.
The updater feed is unchanged by a prerelease publication: latest.json content and the counting-gateway URLs still address the previous stable version, verified in the publish job output.
The publish-cask job is skipped for hyphenated tags and still runs for stable tags.
The existing hyphenated-SemVer prerelease classification (v1.4.0 behavior) keeps working in the create and idempotent-update paths.
Windows assets upload for a prerelease when WINDOWS_RELEASE is set, and the asset digest verification path covers them.
A subsequent stable release on the same pipeline advances releases/latest and the updater feed exactly as before (existing assertions green).

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: actionlint on .github/workflows/release.yml; npm run release:governance; the workflow's own publish-path assertions on a dry-run/manual dispatch; after approval, the first real prerelease tag run serves as live evidence.
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: For the first prerelease tag: release-view JSON with isPrerelease=true and isLatest=false, releases/latest unchanged, latest.json diff-clean, cask job skipped in the run log; for the next stable release: feed-advance and cask assertions green, proving no stable-path regression.

Assumptions.Assumption: Only -beta.N and -canary.N suffix shapes are expected in practice; the classifier keeps treating any hyphenated SemVer as a prerelease.

Testers install prereleases by direct asset links over the stable installation (same bundle id) and roll back by reinstalling the stable DMG; the existing updater rollback guards cover the return path.
The owner accepts collecting-train quality for prerelease tags: the prerelease path deliberately skips train readiness while keeping signing and notarization.
